title: On-demand SKU sensitivity and short-run hosted unit-econ stress test
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a short-run sensitivity analysis for on-demand SKU mixes in the Hosted API product. The goal is to provide an ops + product playbook for surge scenarios where customers exceed baseline usage (e.g., viral growth, marketing spikes) and we must decide which SKU/model/region to route to, what reserve/burst policy to trigger, and what margin impact to expect in the next 7–30 days.

Assumptions (short-run/operational):
- Time horizon: 7–30 days (no long-term capacity purchases).
- On-demand SKUs include: ond-std (spot-lean), ond-plus (on-demand reserved OS), ond-premium (low-latency instance types).
- Pricing and COGS are per-1k tokens for parity with internal reporting.
- We show stress cases for +2x and +5x request volume over baseline for small-to-medium customers.
- We assume existing prefix cache hit rates are unchanged, unless explicitly noted.

Quick summary recommendation (ops):
- For 2x short spikes: prefer ond-plus in region with spare ond-plus capacity; apply aggressive batching for requests >128 tokens and increase prefix cache TTL by 30s where safe.
- For 5x spikes: decline non-critical low-tier inference, spill to ond-std in alternate region with cheaper GPU spot mix, and activate emergency price-signal to customers.
- Enable model fallback (quantized variant) for chat workloads where quality regressions are tolerable.

Spreadsheet snapshot (text table) - single sheet: "short_run_skus"
Columns: Model | Region | SKU | Base COGS ($/1k tokens) | Avg tokens / req | Baseline TPS | Baseline daily calls | 2x daily calls | 5x daily calls | Eff PPK ($/1k) @ baseline | Eff PPK @2x | Eff PPK @5x | Margin % @baseline | Margin % @5x | Notes
Rows (sample):
- Mistral-Chat-8x | us-west1 | ond-plus | 0.045 | 60 | 25 | 2,160,000 | 4,320,000 | 10,800,000 | 0.048 | 0.053 | 0.068 | 42% | 30% | batched well, low latency impact
- Llama2-70B-Quant | eu-west1 | ond-std | 0.023 | 120 | 12 | 1,036,800 | 2,073,600 | 5,184,000 | 0.027 | 0.034 | 0.047 | 55% | 28% | quantized variant increases throughput
- RedWood-Lite-Variant | ap-southeast1 | ond-premium | 0.072 | 40 | 40 | 3,456,000 | 6,912,000 | 17,280,000 | 0.075 | 0.082 | 0.095 | 33% | 10% | high base COGS, latency-sensitive customers

Notes on the table calculations (how Eff PPK changes):
- Eff PPK = base COGS adjusted by observed batching efficiency and marginal queuing penalties. Conservative estimate: batching reduces per-token infra cost by 8% at avg batch size 2–4, 18% at avg batch size 8–16. During heavy spike, batching efficiency degrades linearly as queue time SLO tradeoffs kick in. We model a +10–40% inflation of per-token infra cost when throughput exceeds reserve thresholds.

Micro-sim scenarios (examples):
1) 2x spike, routing policy = latency-first in-region:
   - Outcome: ond-plus in-region handles 70% of demand, secondary region ond-std handles 30% (cross-region egress +$0.003/1k tokens applied).
   - Unit cost change: average eff PPK +12%.
   - Margin move: -8–12 ppts for low-tier customers.
   - Ops action: enable 150ms relaxed latency SLO for non-critical routes, increase batch_window by 40ms.
2) 5x spike, routing policy = cost-first:
   - Outcome: 50% routed to ond-std spot pools, 30% to ond-plus (overflow), 20% dropped/queued to next window or returned 503.
   - Unit cost change: average eff PPK +55%.
   - Margin move: -30–45 ppts; many low-usage customers cross below break-even.
   - Ops action: dynamically throttle free-tier endpoints, send emergency rate-limit notice.

Operational playbook snippets (checklist form):
- Pre-spike: confirm ond-plus spare capacity by region (SRE runbook cmd: check-reserve --region us-west1).
- Early spike detection: traffic delta > 25% in 5m rolling window -> enable batching relaxation rule.
- Mid spike (2x–3x): switch non-SLA traffic to ond-std fallback pool if cost below configured threshold, opt-in customers get soft-notification.
- Severe spike (>3x): enable emergency throttles for anonymous tokens, run autofallback to quantized families, escalate to on-call SRE and send customer comms.

Customer-facing signal experiment (brief):
- Test template: send non-blocking header X-Redwood-Cost-Pressure when PPK > threshold for > 10m. Track if clients change request shape (reduce tokens) after receiving header.
- Hypothesis: 10% of mid-tier customers will reduce average completion length by 15% within 30m of receiving header.

Open questions / RFIs:
- Which models are allowed to be automatically quantized for fallback? (Product + Applied ML decision).
- Are there contractual constraints preventing us from returning 503s for certain enterprise tokens? (Legal/CS ask).
- Can we instrument more granular per-route batching windows in prod without a release? (Infra/Runtime)
